Teaching has been part of my work since high school, and it's the reason I'm pursuing a
Certificate in College Teaching alongside the Ph.D. I've built two courses from nothing,
taught sections of 180+ students, and now run a course of my own.

## Duke University

::: {.entry}
[STA 199: Introduction to Data Science and Statistical Thinking]{.entry-title} [Summer 2026]{.entry-date}
[Department of Statistical Science · *Instructor of Record*]{.entry-meta}

Full responsibility for a core statistics course carrying Duke credit — hand-crafted lectures,
labs, homework, and exams. [Course site](https://sta199-su26-2.github.io/)
:::

## UCLA

::: {.entry}
[Teaching Assistant, Department of Statistics and Data Science]{.entry-title} [Jan – Jun 2024]{.entry-date}
[STATS 13: Introduction to Statistical Methods for Life and Health Sciences]{.entry-meta}
[STATS 102B: Introduction to Computation and Optimization for Statistics]{.entry-meta}

Wrote original homework assignments and practice exams, led office hours and review sessions,

## Courses I built

::: {.entry}
[Math Speeder Upper Course — Introduction to Multivariable Calculus]{.entry-title} [Summer 2021]{.entry-date}
[*Instructor and Curriculum Designer*]{.entry-meta}

A fully online introductory multivariable calculus course: 22 lectures, homework with
solutions, quizzes, two midterms, three projects, and a final exam. Ten students in the first
cohort, and new students still work through the now fully asynchronous material every year.
Built to be accessible to any student regardless of background or socioeconomic status.
:::

::: {.entry}
[Physics Catcher Upper Course — Selected Topics from AP Physics]{.entry-title} [Summer 2020]{.entry-date}
[*Instructor and Curriculum Designer*]{.entry-meta}

A fully online introductory physics course: 17 lectures, homework assignments and answer keys,
a midterm, and a final exam.
:::
